01 / TALKS & WORKSHOPS

Open minds. Change the conversation.

For the big stage. The boardroom. The team that needs a fresh perspective.

Thought-provoking ideas, real business experience and plenty to take back to work.

01AI · Critical thinking · Human potential

AI × HUMAN INTELLIGENCE

The most important upgrade is human.

How do you make people better at working with AI, rather than merely better at using it? Explore the critical thinking, cognitive diversity and human judgement that turn powerful technology into meaningful progress.

02Teams · Collaboration · Culture

THE POWER OF COGNITIVE DIVERSITY

Great minds don’t always think alike.

Different minds see problems differently. Discover what happens when organisations make room for that difference: richer collaboration, better communication and decisions that escape the echo chamber.

03Creativity · Critical thinking · Innovation

DIMENSIONAL THINKING

A different angle changes everything.

Develop HOW people think, not simply what they know. Question. Connect. Challenge. Interpret. Rethink. An invitation to see beyond the obvious and find possibilities hiding in plain sight.

04Talent · Inclusion · Different minds

THINKING DIFFERENTLY ABOUT NEURODIVERSITY

Normal is overrated.

A provocative and practical rethink of talent, ability, difference and what we mean by “normal”. Chris brings business experience and his own lived experience to a conversation that goes beyond awareness.

05Social impact · Purpose · Ethical business

SUPERCHARGING THE S IN ESG

What if doing good was more than a tick box?

An accessible introduction to social impact: what a business changes for people, communities and society. Drawing on Chris’s work as co-founder of My Social Impact, connect purpose with action, evidence and a story worth telling.

06Leadership · Convention · Change

WHAT THE HELL IS NORMAL ANYWAY?

Why Great Leaders Don’t Do Normal

Better leaders don’t simply follow established norms. They challenge convention, question the rules and recognise when it’s time to rewrite them. A fresh perspective on leadership for people ready to think beyond business as usual.

Good thinking works in more than one format.

02 / ABOUT CHRIS

A career that
doesn’t fit
in one box.

Advertising. Strategy. Writing. Social impact. Community festivals. Music. Entrepreneurship. Speaking. Ideas.

Chris’s professional life looks unusually varied. But the same instinct runs through all of it: question the obvious, connect things that don’t normally get connected, and see what happens.

That’s what he means by a Thought Architect. Someone who helps people look again, think beyond the familiar and build a different way forward.

Serious experience.
An enquiring mind.

Over more than 25 years, Chris has worked across advertising, marketing, business, creativity and strategy. A former Creative Director and board director at Saatchi & Saatchi, his work has involved brands including IKEA, Diageo, AOL, Ford, Toyota, Sony and Sky.

He was also a board director of the Direct Marketing Association and chair of its Agencies Council and Creative Council. A Doctor of Business, author, business adviser and entrepreneur, he brings the realities of business into conversations about its future.

His book Ethical Marketing & The New Consumer reflects a longstanding interest in how business behaves. As co-founder of My Social Impact, he helps organisations connect social purpose with meaningful action.

Different thinking is personal.

Chris’s lived experience includes Dyslexia (common among entrepreneurs) and ADHD. His own lived experience informs his interest in creativity, inclusion and the many different ways people think. It’s a personal perspective, not a claim that any two minds work alike.

A CAREER WORKING WITH BRANDS INCLUDING

IKEADiageoAOL.FordTOYOTASONYsky

BEYOND THE CONFERENCE STAGE

Ideas need
room to perform.

A guitar, a live room and the possibility that something unexpected might happen.

Chris’s love of guitar, bands, live performance and improvisation is part of the same story. Listen closely. Make connections. Leave space for someone else to surprise you.

As founder of London Community Arts and Crouch End Festival, he has helped create places where people and ideas meet. He developed The Intimate Space in a 500-year-old church tower in North London, founded üF-Beat Fringe Music Club, developed The Holy Eye venue and created Explore Music More.

His contribution was recognised with the Haringey Community Hero Award 2024. Different stages. The same belief in what people can create together.
